about: The sources a house's research goes through (spec 145 T5), by region: the brief of a house's task, of a municipality's skeleton and of a house's look lists them for the agent — never into the house (only what said something, the one line of what was gone through, and the steps by hand that belong to it). A region is given where its bbox [west, south, east, north] holds the municipality's point (several regions near a border: each, the agent takes its country's); none holds it, or the place has no point: the general list alone. by: agent — the agent goes through it itself, as the terms strom enforces allow (strom net web --check <url>); hand — only the person can (a site that refuses automated reading, an archive's reading room): a link with what to do, written only where it belongs to the house. town: the skeleton's (once for a municipality); house: each house's; special: a mill, an inn, a smithy, a parish, a school besides; look: the look of a house. Only what is known for sure of a region is in it.

town.what: printed topographies and gazetteers of the 18th and 19th century of the region: the municipality, its lordship, its mills, farms and solitudes
the field names of the municipality with their points (mills, farms, solitudes, fields): written once as its field names
town.where: the country's open gazetteer of names

town.what: the municipality's web, its chronicle, its Wikipedia page: its history, its mills, its fires
pictures of the municipality under a free licence (the green, its streets, a house number where it can be read): each with its licence and what it shows
town.where: Wikimedia Commons, Europeana, the municipality's web

town.what: the oldest cadastral maps of the cadastral area: their sheets

house.what: the address and building of today in the country's open address register: its point, the building, its parcel
the orthophoto of today and old aerial photos: does the old building stand, a farmstead
what the municipality's skeleton has of this number: the topography, a field name at its point
local websites about the houses (the municipality's, a local history society's)
the land registers of the estate (holders, purchase contracts)

special.what: other buildings of the same kind in the municipality (a second mill explains 'the miller in another number')
a mill: its water course and its mill race
where the holder came from: the same craft of the family in the neighbouring places

look.what: the old aerial photo at the house's point: the building, its outbuildings, its yard
the municipality's pictures of its skeleton: one that shows this house (its number, its place on the green)
the material at the house or its municipality nobody has read: a sketch, a photo, a clip of a map
the sources in hand that describe the building: a cottage, a farm, a fire, a rebuilding, a mill

the municipality's web, its chronicle, its Wikipedia page
pictures of the municipality under a free licence: each with its licence and what it shows
town.where: Wikimedia Commons, Kramerius (free works), Europeana, the municipality's web

town.what: the listed monuments of the municipality with their house numbers
the map sheets of the stable cadastre of the cadastral area (which sheet holds which part): a link by hand with the sheet numbers
the land registers of the estate online
town.where: SOA Praha eBadatelna, Porta fontium (SOA Plzeň), MZA's ARON
